headline: Local Man Sentenced to One-Day Police Custody for Being Too Polite During Cross-Examination
body:
A local man, Rakesh Sharma, was remanded to one-day police custody on Tuesday after a Delhi court found his persistent use of the phrase 'Ji, bilkul' during cross-examination to be a deliberate attempt to lull the prosecution into a state of hypnotic comfort. The presiding magistrate ordered the detention, noting that Mr. Sharma’s ability to remain unflappably courteous while being grilled by the complainant’s counsel was not only irregular but bordered on tactical psychological warfare.

'I have sat on this bench for fifteen years, and I have never seen a witness agree with every single leading question with such terrifyingly genuine warmth,' the magistrate noted while signing the remand order. 'By constantly nodding and asking if the lawyers needed a glass of water, the defendant effectively dismantled the adversarial nature of the court, leaving the prosecution with no one to argue against.'

Legal experts suggest this is the first time a defendant has been detained primarily to 'lower his agreeability levels' before the trial resumes. The complainant’s lawyer, who had initially sought a standard detention, expressed relief at the court’s decision. 'He was being so helpful that I actually started to forget why I was suing him in the first place,' the lawyer admitted, visibly shaken. 'If he continues to be this reasonable, the entire legal system risks collapsing into a series of friendly conversations.'

Mr. Sharma is expected to spend the next 24 hours in a cell designed specifically to harden his demeanor, where he will be required to listen to at least six hours of aggressive call-center training tapes to ensure he stops saying 'thank you' to the constables when they bring him his dinner.
